skill.name: artifacts-builder
skill.description: Creates multi-component Claude HTML artifacts with React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, Vite, and Parcel.
skill.summary: Initialize, develop, and bundle complex React applications as self-contained HTML artifacts.
skill.author: ArtemisAI

security_audit.summary: All 29 static findings are false positives involving expected shell setup, local configuration edits, Markdown formatting, or documentation URLs. Semantic review found command injection risk from unescaped project names and supply chain exposure from automatic, unpinned package installation. Publication should wait until project name handling and dependency installation are hardened.

remediation.issue: Project names are interpolated into a sed expression.
remediation.suggestion: Validate names with a strict allowlist. Pass the title through an environment variable to a structured HTML or JavaScript editor.

remediation.issue: The scripts install and execute mutable registry packages automatically.
remediation.suggestion: Require pnpm instead of installing it globally. Pin package versions and enforce lockfile integrity before running package lifecycle scripts.

semantic_findings.title: Unescaped Project Name Enables sed Injection
semantic_findings.description: The first script argument is interpolated directly into a sed program. Crafted delimiters or flags can alter the program and may trigger command execution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: PROJECT_NAME comes from the first argument and reaches a sed expression without escaping. sed replacement delimiters and executable flags make this a credible injection path.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Mutable Dependency Execution
semantic_findings.description: The scripts globally install pnpm and execute many unpinned registry packages. A compromised or changed package could run lifecycle code on the host.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited commands explicitly install global, latest, and otherwise unpinned packages. Package managers can execute dependency lifecycle scripts during installation.

content.user_title: Build Complex React Artifacts for Claude
content.value_statement: Complex HTML artifacts need more structure than a single file can provide. This skill scaffolds a React project and bundles it into shareable HTML.
actual_capabilities: Creates a React 18 and TypeScript project with Vite.
Configures Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui theming, and source path aliases.
Installs Radix UI and supporting frontend dependencies.
Extracts more than 40 bundled shadcn/ui components into the project.
Selects a Vite version based on the installed Node.js major version.
Bundles project assets into a self-contained bundle.html file.
limitations: Requires Bash, Node.js 18 or newer, npm, and network access for packages.
Runs package installation commands and writes configuration files in the project.
Targets a fixed React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Vite, and Parcel stack.
Does not provide automated tests or verify the final artifact by default.

best_practices: Use this skill for artifacts that need multiple components, routes, or coordinated state.
Review generated dependencies and configuration changes before running the scripts.
Test bundle.html in a browser before sharing the final artifact.
anti_patterns: Do not use this stack for a small artifact that fits in one HTML file.
Do not pass untrusted or unusual characters as the project name.
Do not run the bundler from a directory containing unrelated dist or bundle.html files.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a configured React and TypeScript project, then bundles the project into one HTML file.

faq.question: Which Node.js versions are supported?
faq.answer: The initialization script requires Node.js 18 or newer and selects a compatible Vite version.

faq.question: Does the skill require internet access?
faq.answer: Yes. The scripts install project and bundling dependencies from package registries.

faq.question: Can it bundle an existing project?
faq.answer: Yes, when the project has package.json and a root index.html compatible with the bundling commands.

faq.question: Which interface components are included?
faq.answer: The archive includes more than 40 shadcn/ui components and the script installs their supporting dependencies.

faq.question: Does it test the final artifact?
faq.answer: No. Testing is optional, so you should verify the generated bundle in a browser before sharing it.
